turns.realization: Magpie keeps her eyes on the guard's gold watch while she pushes food around her tray. "Pretty things never stay pretty in here for long."
Magpie murmurs to Ivy, "Whatever happened to that nurse who kept staring at our table last month?"
Magpie flicks a glance at Harley. "You want a distraction. She wants a favor. I'm listening to both of you."
Magpie notes the scratched tag on the guard's key ring without staring. "East stairwell must be popular."
Magpie whispers, "If I help you move that packet, you don't sell me to Harley when it goes wrong."
Magpie smiles without warmth. "What would you trade for a guard looking the wrong way for ten seconds?"
Magpie palms the mess hall token under the tray. "Little things buy bigger mistakes in Arkham."
Magpie kicks a ceramic shard aside. "Someone's going to blame us for this mess unless we move."
Magpie raises her hands. "We could all eat in peace if nobody plays hero today. What do you say?"
Magpie leans back. "Nobody's walking out of here clean. Stop pretending otherwise."
Magpie stands as guards approach. "If you're moving us, say where. I don't like surprises."
Magpie shuffles in the transfer line, eyes on the corridor cameras. "Mess hall's done. What's next—punishment or opportunity?"
Magpie forces a laugh. "We're all victims here, right? Maybe we stop biting each other."
Magpie looks at Ivy, not Harley. "I kept your secret. That means something, even in here."
When a guard snaps at Ivy, Magpie says nothing—but her jaw tightens. Ivy notices.
Magpie mutters, "Harley wants a riot. You want a garden. I want to survive the corridor."
Magpie repeats quietly, "Pretty things don't stay pretty." She watches Harley's reaction.
Magpie asks the guard, "Did the nurse who reported you get reassigned—or disappeared?"
Magpie fingers the token. "This buys a door. Question is whose door you want opened."
Magpie nods at the scratched key tag. "East stairwell. That's where trouble lives."
Magpie doesn't soften her voice. "If you sell me out, I'll make sure you regret it before lights-out."
Magpie lets the guards hurry her along. "This isn't over. It's just moving rooms."
